lesson.title: Product classification case
lesson.summary: Apply the full product-route test to changed facts while retaining separate scope and date checks.

prerequisites.reason: The product case requires the final safety-component rule including its failure qualification.
The case must distinguish classification from the provisions that apply to the sector.
The product case must establish the mandatory third-party condition with evidence. The case includes a route required solely because of a non-health/safety risk.

blocks: **Product-route assessment** combines function, listed coverage and required assessment. We use a fictional protective device. Stipulated facts: it is covered by a current Annex I instrument, AI fulfils its safety function, and the product must undergo third-party assessment for health and safety risks.
These are supplied case facts, not a sector classification derived by this lesson. Record them and their evidence in a real assessment.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(1), 6(1a)–(1c); Annex I; Article 2(2)

blocks: On those facts, both paragraph 1 conditions are met. The solely non-safety-function limit does not fit a genuine protective function, and paragraph 1c does not remove a health/safety assessment route.
The conclusion is high-risk by the product route. It still requires separate examination of Article 2 sector limits, prohibition facts, applicable obligations and dates.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(1), 6(1a)–(1c); Annex I; Article 2(2)

blocks: Changed fact: the AI now changes display colours only, with evidence that its failure has no safety effect. Paragraph 1a may remove safety-component status. But check whether the AI is itself a covered product; paragraph 1(a) has that alternative.
Changed fact: a claimed convenience feature's failure disables protection. Paragraph 1b restores safety-component status. Assess actual failure consequences rather than relabelling the feature.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(1), 6(1a)–(1c); Annex I; Article 2(2)

blocks: Changed fact: only voluntary external testing is documented. The required-assessment condition is not established. The sound record names that gap rather than assuming the same result.
A conclusion should state which route was tested, which facts were stipulated or verified, and which conclusions remain open. Annex III can still matter where a separate listed use is present.

questions.prompt: The fictional case establishes listed coverage, an AI safety function and a required safety assessment. What is the Article 6 route result?

options.reason: The stipulated facts meet the cumulative product-route test.

options.blocks: Excluded because an AI component is separately supplied
options.reason: Independent supply does not remove the paragraph 1 test.

options.blocks: Exempt because a user operates it
options.reason: Human operation is not a product-route exemption.

variants.prompt: With both product-route conditions established and no stated qualification removing them, what classification follows?

options.blocks: Excluded because an AI component is separately supplied
options.reason: Independent supply does not remove the paragraph 1 test.

options.blocks: Exempt because a user operates it
options.reason: Human operation is not a product-route exemption.

questions.prompt: The component is renamed 'convenience', but its failure disables protection. Which fact controls this part of the test?

options.reason: A name cannot negate the failure evidence.

options.blocks: Only the colour of the interface
options.reason: Appearance does not resolve safety-component status.

variants.prompt: Can a convenience label exclude a component whose malfunction endangers safety?

options.blocks: Only the colour of the interface

An optional test is not proof of a mandatory route.

options.reason: The statutory condition specifically concerns required assessment.
